name: Aria Amazon

seo.title: Aria Amazon Cruise from Nauta, Peru | James Wild & Co
seo.description: Aria Amazon by Aqua Expeditions: 16 suites, 32 guests, 26 crew. Three, four or seven nights from Nauta into Peru's Pacaya-Samiria reserve.

tagline: Sixteen suites with floor-to-ceiling glass, three decks, and the Marañón outside.
answer: Aria Amazon is Aqua Expeditions' 16-suite riverboat in the Peruvian Amazon. She carries 32 guests with 26 crew and sails three, four or seven nights round trip from Nauta, near Iquitos, on the Marañón and Ucayali rivers into the Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve. She suits couples and families who want a short, well-run river trip.
overview: Aria Amazon was designed by Jordi Puig and custom built for the Peruvian Amazon. She is the sister ship to Aqua Nera and carries 32 guests in 16 river-facing suites across three decks, with 26 crew.

Every suite is the same design suite for two, with a king or twin beds, a daybed by floor-to-ceiling windows and a walk-in rain shower. Suites 103 and 105, and 104 and 106, connect. The top deck holds the shared spaces, with views all round. Excursions run from the first deck.
why: One suite type means no upsell and no bad cabin.

inclusions: Entrance fee to the Pacaya-Samiria Reserve
faqs: Round trip from Nauta, about two hours from Iquitos, on the Marañón, Ucayali and Amazon rivers in and around the Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve in Peru.
Three, four or seven nights. The 3-night Discovery works the Marañón side; the 4-night Explorer goes up the Ucayali to Dorado and Clavero lakes.
Aqua Expeditions publishes fares sailing by sailing. Those still to sail are under Dates and rates; for later dates, ask us.
All 16 are the same design suite for two, with floor-to-ceiling windows, a daybed, a walk-in rain shower and king or twin beds. Four connect in pairs.
Fly Lima to Iquitos; Aqua meets guests at its airport counter and transfers them to Nauta for a 4:30pm boarding.

suits.line: One suite type, all with the same window.
Three nights is enough to see the reserve's edge.
